subject: Culture
title: Ayodhya Dispute
description: Learn Ayodhya Dispute in one minute.

hook.text: In 1992 a Hindu mob demolished the Babri Masjid mosque in Ayodhya, India. Riots killed over 2,000 people.

buildup.text: Hindus claimed the mosque was built on the birthplace of Lord Ram. Muslims said it was their mosque since 1528.

discovery.text: Archaeology found temple remnants beneath the mosque. Both sides claimed the evidence proved their case.

twist.text: In 2019 India's Supreme Court awarded the site to Hindus and gave Muslims alternate land—satisfying neither fully.

climax.text: A new Ram temple opened in 2024 on the site, reopening wounds some hoped the verdict had closed.

punchline.text: Sacred ground never forgets who was there first—or second.

quiz.question: When was the Babri Masjid demolished?

details.summary: The Ayodhya dispute — a centuries-long conflict over a site in India sacred to both Hindus and Muslims — culminated when a mob demolished the Babri Masjid mosque in 1992, triggering riots that killed over 2,000 people. In 2019, India's Supreme Court awarded the site to Hindus for a Ram temple.
details.whyItMatters: Ayodhya represents how sacred space disputes can escalate into lethal violence and reshape national politics. The conflict transformed Indian politics and Hindu-Muslim relations for decades.
takeaways: Hindus believe Ayodhya is the birthplace of the god Ram
The Babri Masjid mosque was demolished by Hindu nationalists in 1992
India's Supreme Court awarded the site for a Hindu temple in 2019

faq.question: What is the Ayodhya dispute about?
faq.answer: Hindus believe a site in Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh, is the exact birthplace of Lord Ram. The Mughal emperor Babur built a mosque (Babri Masjid) there in 1528, possibly on the ruins of a Hindu temple.

faq.question: What happened after the Babri Masjid demolition?
faq.answer: The 1992 demolition triggered Hindu-Muslim riots across India killing over 2,000 people, mostly Muslims. The event radicalized both communities and transformed Indian politics — the BJP, which supported the Ram temple movement, rose to national power.
